A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SignGD and transformer study. Their main text, figures, equations, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures and unchanged proofs.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic training-dynamics experiments and noisy MNIST classification results, including optimizer comparisons and supplementary data-assumption tests.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds multi-head, deeper-transformer, and Adam hyperparameter experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The central model, logistic objective, and SignGD updates remain unchanged. Appendix F.4 adds an explicit constant-H multi-head extension with separately parameterized heads whose outputs are summed, constituting a limited model extension.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic signal/noise classification, sparse/non-sparse and orthogonal/non-orthogonal variants, longer contexts, and noisy MNIST digits 3 versus 7. The additions vary architectures and optimizer settings within this coverage; the larger MNIST sample changes the protocol.

E2.justification: The evaluated optimizer comparison methods remain SignGD, Adam, and GD. The new beta2 sweeps and architectural ablations vary configurations without introducing another baseline method.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 changes MNIST training size from 128 to 2,000 examples and SignGD/Adam learning rates from 5e-4 to 1e-2. GD changes from 200 to 500 epochs and gains SNR-dependent learning rates. New experiments introduce four-head models, two/three attention-block configurations with MLP/residual controls, and Adam beta2 sweeps.

E4.justification: New Appendices B.5–B.7 test whether the four-stage dynamics survive multiple heads, greater depth, MLPs, and residual connections, and investigate which Adam moment parameter explains departures from SignGD. Figures 13–17 and Tables 4–11 provide substantial new sensitivity and failure-mode evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three MNIST runs and report means and standard deviations. V2 introduces no new repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice; additional sign-count tables follow the existing reporting approach.

E6.justification: Figure 2(d) reports changed MNIST test-loss curves under the revised protocol, so these are replaced results rather than same-setting gains. New results document multi-head dynamics, architectural effects on alignment and stability, and beta2-dependent convergence and update decay. Table 2 and the original supplementary plots are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix F.4 adds the multi-head mathematical formulation and an argument that a constant number of heads preserves the early-stage scaling needed for the four-stage analysis. Condition 3.1, Theorem 3.2, Appendices C–E, and the existing extensions F.1–F.3 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same core claims: four-stage SignGD dynamics, fast convergence with poor generalization, similarities to Adam, and greater sensitivity to noisy data than GD.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations involving beta2-driven update decay, gradient shrinkage and numerical precision in deeper models, and possible rank-collapse effects without residuals. Appendix H newly qualifies transfer to real-world transformers through differences in noise structure, GD optimization difficulty, and the meaning of robustness.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 revises the documented MNIST training recipe, including sample size, learning rates, and budgets. The new studies specify head counts, depth/MLP/residual configurations, and beta2 settings. These provide additional reproducibility information without a broader implementation or resource-release addition.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting feature learning, practical query-key attention, Adam second-moment robustness, and rank collapse, including Dong et al. and Noci et al. The related-work discussion expands locally while retaining the original research positioning and novelty claim.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 receives a clearer stage-by-stage explanation with explicit time intervals and a clarification of negative noise. V2 adds explanatory appendices, acknowledgments, and publication headers, while retaining the main section order and most existing prose.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned into five stage-focused panels; its earlier display survives as v2 Figure 3. Figure 2 adds key-signal curves and revises the MNIST panel. New architectural and optimizer plot grids, Tables 4–11, and the annotated timeline in Figure 19 substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V1 left richer architectures untested and explained Adam's departures largely through a momentum conjecture. V2's architectural ablations and controlled beta2 studies substantially strengthen this central empirical connection and reveal its failure conditions; Appendix H also makes practical applicability more explicit. These gains and clearer dynamics visualizations outweigh a local inconsistency in B.7, where the sentence about small beta2 preventing alignment reverses the trend shown in Figure 17.
